summary: Wai-lun Tam specializes in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara and served as professor and Department Chairperson in Cultural and Religious Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Walpola Rahula (1907–1997) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar. He studied at Vidyalankara Pirivena, Calcutta, Ceylon under G. P. Malalasekera, and Paris/Sorbonne under Paul Demiéville. He held posts at Northwestern, Sri Jayewardenepura, and Oxford.

Walter Bruno Henning (1908–1967) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at the University of Göttingen (~1926–1930), he held posts at the University of London and SOAS (~1936–1961), Columbia (~1946–1947), and UC Berkeley (~1961–1967).

Walter Elliot (1803–1887) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at East India Company College (~1818–1820) and the College of Fort St George (~1820–1823), later serving as Private Secretary in the Madras Government (1837–1842).

Walter Eugene Clark (1881–1960) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Harvard (A.B., Doctorate) and under Richard Pischel, he held posts at the University of Chicago (1915–1927) and served as Harvard's Wales Professor of Sanskrit (1927–1950).

Walter Liebenthal (1886–1982) was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Breslau (Dr. phil) and elsewhere under Nobel, Walleser, and Strauss, he held posts at Peking University (1937), Visva-Bharati, Sorbonne, and the University of Tübingen (1965–1982).

Walter M. Spink (1928–2019) worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Amherst College (~1945–1949) and Harvard University (~1949–1954, PhD), he taught at Brandeis University (1956–1961) and the University of Michigan (~1961–2000).

Walter Nowick (1926–2013) was a Buddhist studies practitioner and teacher. He studied at the Juilliard School and under Zuigan Goto (1950–1965), held a post at Kyoto Women's University, and founded Moonspring Hermitage.

Walter Porzig (1895–1961) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Jena (~1913–1920) and under Wilhelm Streitberg (~1919–1921), holding posts at Leipzig (~1921–1925), Bern (~1925–1935), Jena (~1935–1945), and Mainz (~1951–1961).

Walter Ruben (1899–1982) specialized in Indology. He held academic posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1931–1935), the University of Chile (~1948–1949), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1950–1965).

Walter Simon (1893–1981) worked in sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. Educated at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke and August Hermann Francke, he held posts at Berlin (1919–1937) and SOAS / University of London (1936–1960), including Professor of Chinese.

Walter Slaje (1954–) is an Indologist who completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna. His career includes posts at Graz University Library (1984–1995) and serving as Director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2019).

Walter William Skeat (1835–1912) was an English linguist. He was educated at King's College School, Highgate School, and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1854–1858), and later held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1878–1912).

Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz (1878–1965) specialized in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Stanford University (~1902–1907), Jesus College, Oxford (1907), and was a disciple of Kazi Dawa Samdup (~1919–1922).

Walther Heissig (1913–2005) specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies. Educated at Vienna, Berlin, Göttingen, and Bonn, he lectured at Peking University (~1941–1945) and Fu Jen Catholic University, later serving as Central Asian seminar chair at Bonn (1964).

Walther Schubring (1881–1969) was an Indologist who studied at Munich and Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann. Following a post at the Royal Library of Berlin (1907), he held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg from 1920 to 1951.

Walther Wüst (1901–1993) worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich, where he served as Privatdozent (1932) and Dean of the Faculty of Philosophy (1935–1945), later holding posts at Ahnenerbe and Deutsche Akademie.
Wang Pachow (1918–2012) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He studied under Tan Yun-shan and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

Wannaporn Rienjang is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Cambridge. She has held posts at the British Museum, the University of Oxford (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).

Warren Crawford Cowgill (1929–1985) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and earned his Ph.D. at Yale University (~1952–1957), where he became professor of linguistics in 1956.
